rule: When a fix changes a value's null-ness (e.g. `x || default` -> explicit null check, or `?? default`), grep EVERY downstream consumer of that variable for unguarded use and add the guard in the SAME fix. If a consumer can't be guarded here, mark the fix 'skipped'.
why: Removing a fallback coercion at the assignment site leaves downstream consumers that assumed the value was never null/undefined. Generic lesson, confirmed in the MLX pipeline (count or 1 -> None crash).

rule: Do not broaden catch/finally to swallow errors silently. A missing dependency or environment error must stay LOUD (propagate, or log + degrade). Narrow catches to the specific error class.
why: except/catch over-reach is the #1 error-handling fix defect; silent swallowing hides environment failures the operator must see.

rule: GUI review-lane findings are ~50% false-positive. Before applying any fix, grep the cited symbol's ACTUAL usage and scan ~70 lines for existing guards. Do not trust the finding's own claim or the adversarial verifier (it re-derives from the same flawed premise).
why: 2026-06-19 batch: 4/8 FP (lora.path framed as a leak but it's functional identity; subprocess getReader already guarded). The lane's adversarial verify reported upheld=0 yet findings stayed 'verified'.

rule: A finding can have a REAL symptom but the WRONG root-cause location. Chase the symptom to its real offender before fixing the blamed file.
why: Generic across both review lanes; a HIGH finding often blames the correct sentinel while the real bug is in a consumer.

rule: A finding's symptom can be entirely FABRICATED. For any finding claiming a runtime behavior ('X silently does Y'), trace the ACTUAL code path to confirm the behavior can happen at all before judging the fix.
why: The adversarial verifier cannot catch a fabricated symptom — it re-derives plausibility from the same flawed premise. Code-level tracing beats the verifier.

rule: The restore record carries the ACTUAL reverted file list. Pass it into the report verbatim; the report must never infer or guess which file was reverted.
why: A report LLM given only a count will hallucinate the file (MLX iter-6 named the wrong file).

rule: restoreTriggered:true is NOT a success signal. After restore, independently confirm the suite/build is green and surface that result in the report.
why: The flag only means a revert was attempted; it has coexisted with both green and still-red trees.

rule: Report recommendations must reflect the ACTUAL final tree state, never assumptions about what was reverted. If a recommendation says 're-attempt X', first confirm X is not already in the tree.
why: iter-6 recommendation #5 said 're-attempt require_ffmpeg' but it had already shipped that run.
